newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U sees ex-Sweden air freight 700-800 tonnes '97.
newsitem.headline: P&U sees ex-Sweden air freight 700-800 tonnes '97.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn (P&U) said on Tuesday it expected to ship 700 to 800 tonnes of its drugs by air in 1997, about the same it shipped the year before.
"In 1996 we shipped between 700 to 800 tonnes and we have the same figures forecast for 1997," P&U Sweden distribution manager Jan Pettersson told Reuters.
However, he said in general he expected the company's need to ship by air cargo would increase because of the trend to ship products on demand instead of storing them in warehouses.
"It's a matter of capital rationalisation. The goods should be on their way, not stored in warehouses," he said.
Air cargo capacity from Sweden was more or less in balance with demand for space, with perhaps a bit of overcapacity, Pettersson said.

The company's main production plants are in the Stockholm area, and Swedish cities Uppsala and Helsingborg. Its customers are around the world, but Pettersson said the most important markets were Europe, the United States and Asia.
From these sites the air cargo shipments are taken by truck to Stockholm's international airport at Arlanda.
The company does not ship all its drugs by air.
"We don't ship all the drugs everytime...preferably it's small volumes with high value," Pettersson said.
